requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook create-ca.yml generated an RSA CA key, CSR, and self-signed x509 CA certificate via community.crypto on node1. Playbook run completed with 7 changed/ok tasks and no failures. openssl x509 on the resulting certificate confirms subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA with critical Basic Constraints CA:TRUE and a 10-year validity window, matching the required name exactly.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: The CA cert was copied into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and update-ca-certificates was run as part of the same playbook. openssl verify against /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt returns OK, and the CA subject is found by grepping the system trust bundle. A re-run of the playbook shows the update-ca-certificates task correctly skipped (idempotent), confirming the trust installation persisted as expected without needing repeated work.

Ansible and the community.crypto collection were installed on node1, a playbook (create-ca.yml) was written using ansible.builtin and community.crypto modules to perform key generation, CSR, self-signing, file placement, and update-ca-certificates, then executed locally via ansible-playbook with a full, successful PLAY RECAP.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task contract: a local CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' was generated on node1 via an Ansible playbook using community.crypto, and its certificate was correctly installed into the system trust store with update-ca-certificates, verified by openssl and idempotency re-run. The separate, mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also well executed for both node1 and node2, with clear pre-restart boot identity, acknowledged reboot, changed post-restart boot identity, and confirmed recovery of the CA/trust state on node1 (matching checksums, still verified) and healthy systemd state on node2. No unjustified mutations or residue were found.
limitations: Restart evidence for node2 confirms general system health (systemctl is-system-running) but node2 carries no CA-specific state since the task only targets node1, so its post-restart check is necessarily generic.
No independent verification outside the executor's own commands was possible; assessment relies entirely on the captured command outputs and fixed lifecycle snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace: apt-get install of ansible + ca-certificates (cmd-5b63f564734a415a) is a necessary prerequisite for the Ansible-based implementation. The playbook and its generated key/CSR/cert material were written to /tmp/ansible-ca (cmd-e0e6495ded744415), a bounded, low-risk location; the after-executor temporary-files snapshot no longer lists this directory (it was cleared across the node1 reboot), so no residue remains. The provider-wide restart protocol (reboot of node1 and node2) is outside the public task contract but was executed as an independent, mandated step, not a task-relevant mutation requiring justification here, and both reboots were bounded and fully recovered. No unnecessary, destructive, or unjustified state-changing commands were found among the 21 executed commands; the 5 non-zero-return commands are explained by expected SSH disconnects during reboot and normal 'inactive'/absent-file checks, not failures.
